skill.name: software-testing-router
skill.description: Choose testing methods for CLI, API, web, Qt, and Windows desktop applications using observable capabilities and explicit acceptance criteria.
skill.summary: Route software tests to suitable interfaces, automate scoped Windows UIA actions, and report evidence with clear coverage limits.
skill.author: hunxuankai

security_audit.summary: All 101 static findings are false positives in the reviewed context, including scoped automation, research citations, readable multilingual documentation, and serialized test evidence. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, unauthorized network transmission, or malicious execution. The helper can change the selected application and writes local evidence, so users must authorize test actions and protect artifacts.

content.value_statement: Unclear testing interfaces can lead to fragile automation and incomplete acceptance evidence. This skill selects suitable routes and provides scoped Windows UIA automation with explicit results.
actual_capabilities: Select CLI, API, DOM, Windows UIA, Qt, or visual testing routes based on acceptance criteria and observed interfaces.
Probe verified Windows launcher descendants to identify visible window owners without performing application actions.
Inspect process-scoped UIA controls and supported patterns with configurable depth and node limits.
Execute validated UIA set, invoke, and wait steps with unique selectors, ancestor scopes, and per-step windows.
Apply a worker hard timeout and recover completed steps or unknown action outcomes from durable local journals.
Guide business-result checks, artifact verification, and honest reporting of unsupported or unverified behavior.
limitations: The desktop helper requires Windows, PowerShell 7, Python 3.10 or later, and an interactive desktop.
The helper supports only ValuePattern set, InvokePattern invoke, and selected property waits; it does not automate passwords or global input.
Development tests, fixtures, browser traces, and full reproduction tooling are not included in the installed runtime package.
Historical examples do not establish universal compatibility, visual correctness, or speed gains; several platforms and desktop environments remain unverified.

use_cases.title: Plan Evidence-Based Acceptance Tests
use_cases.description: Map required behaviors to available interfaces and define the minimum evidence needed for each acceptance criterion.

use_cases.title: Test a Windows Executable Without Source
use_cases.description: Identify the correct window owner, inspect available UIA patterns, and validate a scoped workflow against fresh output artifacts.

use_cases.title: Verify Web Export Workflows
use_cases.description: Use actual DOM interactions, scoped selectors, response checks, and exported content to verify asynchronous forms and duplicate buttons.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Testing Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [application] and [acceptance criterion]. Identify available interfaces, recommend a testing route, and state the evidence required. Do not change application state.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: select a method before building automation.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Windows Test Target
prompt_templates.prompt: For [verified PID] and [executable path], plan a read-only UIA probe and shallow inspection. Report window ownership, supported patterns, and ambiguous controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: determine desktop automation capabilities without issuing application actions.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Real Web Button
prompt_templates.prompt: Test [button workflow] at [authorized test URL] using existing tooling. Use unique DOM selectors and verify the request, business result, and fresh artifact.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: distinguish successful UI interaction from direct API success.

prompt_templates.title: Recover an Interrupted UIA Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [UIA report] and [journal] after a timeout. Separate completed steps from unknown outcomes. Check current state before proposing further authorized actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: investigate partial execution without blindly replaying side effects.

output_examples.input: Choose a test route for an export button in a source-free Windows executable.
output: Recommended route: inspect the verified window owner and available UIA patterns.
Execution plan: locate unique input and export controls, perform authorized actions, and wait for an observable completion state.
Required evidence: reopen a fresh exported file and compare its contents with independent expectations.
Coverage limit: successful pattern calls do not prove keyboard shortcuts or visual layout.

output_examples.input: A UIA worker timed out after starting an export. Decide whether to repeat the action.
output: Action outcome: unknown until the journal and current application state are checked.
Recovery step: retain completed steps and inspect the expected artifact or task status.
Retry decision: do not repeat a potentially completed export without confirming the operation's retry safety.
Report status: record the timeout and unverified outcome separately from successful assertions.

output_examples.input: An export API returns HTTP 200, but its business response reports failure.
output: Result: the business assertion fails despite the successful HTTP transport status.
Evidence: preserve the response, relevant interface state, and any contradictory output artifacts.
Coverage note: a direct API call cannot establish that the export button works.

best_practices: Define the acceptance behavior first, then probe existing interfaces and reuse suitable project tooling.
Use unique selectors, explicit target identity, fresh test data, and both condition budgets and a worker hard timeout.
Review journals after interruption and protect logs, reports, traces, and screenshots before sharing them.
anti_patterns: Replacing a required button interaction with a direct API call and reporting the interface as tested.
Selecting the first matching control or guessing coordinates to conceal ambiguous target discovery.
Replaying side-effecting actions after a timeout without checking the journal and actual business outcome.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The package declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Actual execution also requires suitable local tools and permissions.

faq.question: Does Windows desktop testing require application source code?
faq.answer: No. The UIA helper can inspect a running executable when its controls expose suitable accessibility patterns.

faq.question: Can the desktop helper run on macOS or Linux?
faq.answer: No. The bundled UIA backend requires Windows and PowerShell 7. Other testing guidance depends on the project's available environment.

faq.question: Does the skill install test frameworks automatically?
faq.answer: No automatic installer is included. The guidance favors existing tooling and requires deliberate preparation of any missing test dependencies.

faq.question: Does a successful UIA invocation prove business success?
faq.answer: No. An invocation can only confirm dispatch. Verify observable postconditions and the actual output artifact before reporting acceptance.

faq.question: What happens when the UIA worker times out?
faq.answer: The wrapper stops its PowerShell worker, preserves the target application, and recovers journal progress. Started actions may still have unknown business outcomes.
